issues_confirmed: Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:88 writes displayElement.innerHTML unconditionally on every updateDisplay(); the MutationObserver at content.js:120-125 observes document.documentElement with childList+subtree+characterData and therefore sees that write. Observer delivery is a microtask and microtasks queued during a drain run in the same drain, so this is an unbounded feedback loop for as long as the 'Est. wait' text is present. The sibling title write at :82 is guarded; the innerHTML write is not.

Ctrl_Click_New_Tab/content.js:39-40 matches a[href] before any SPA fallback, so ordinary anchors are routed through window.open(url, '_blank') at :58. Native Ctrl+Click opens a background tab; window.open focuses it, so every normal Ctrl+Click on every site (matches <all_urls>) becomes a focus steal.
Ctrl_Click_New_Tab/content.js:40 falls back to anchor.href when getAttribute('href') is empty, so <a href=""> resolves to the current page URL and Ctrl+Click opens a duplicate of the page you are on.
playback_speed_controller/manifest.json:20-22 maps playback.png to the "128" icon key, but `file` reports the asset is 24 x 24 PNG RGBA.
playback_speed_controller/manifest.json:6-8 declares action with default_title only and no default_icon, while background.js:1 makes the toolbar click the sole way to toggle the panel.

playback_speed_controller/background.js:9-20 re-injects content.js via chrome.scripting on sendMessage failure, but content.js has no re-entry guard; setInterval at content.js:328 and the document keydown listener registered inside createUI at content.js:293 would both be duplicated.

Waitlist wait-text regex diverged: Waitlist_Display_Chrome/content.js:67 matches 'person' only, Waitlist_Display_Firefox/content.js:5 matches 'person|people'. The Chrome build shows nothing once the site pluralises.
Waitlist title format diverged: Chrome content.js:54 renders '⏳ N', Firefox content.js:31 assigns the bare number as document.title with no marker.
Waitlist URL scope diverged: Waitlist_Display_Chrome/manifest.json:12 matches all of https://www.mindvideo.ai/*, Waitlist_Display_Firefox/manifest.json:11 matches only /text-to-video/*.
Waitlist_Display_Chrome/manifest.json:17-19 declares a background service_worker whose file (service_worker.js) contains only two comment lines; MV3 does not require a background script.
Waitlist_Display_Firefox/manifest.json:18 still carries the placeholder Gecko id 'queue-wait-tab-title@your-domain.com'.

Auto_Scroll_shorts/content.js:284 calls tryClickNextOverlayButton on the 1300ms timer with no playback-position check; its filter at :206 is /next|episode/i over textContent against the broad selector list at :196-204, so a matching control is clicked on page arrival rather than at end-of-video.

Auto_Scroll_shorts/manifest.json:8 matches only https://www.youtube.com/* and https://goku.sx/*, but content.js:31 and :36 accept any youtube.com host and any *.goku.sx host, making those permissive checks unreachable on m.youtube.com / www.goku.sx.

verdict: Working and genuinely useful; closer to finished than to unfinished. Five small extensions, all syntactically sound, no dependency rot and no build step to break. What stands in the way of 'done' is not missing features but two confirmed defects in code that already exists - the Waitlist Chrome badge spinning its own observer, and Ctrl_Click_New_Tab overreaching onto ordinary links across <all_urls> - plus a README that points at a folder name and an extension that no longer exist. That is roughly two focused hours. The one structural loose end is the duplicated Waitlist codebase, where each fork holds a fix the other lacks; collapsing it to one shared content.js (not a build pipeline) is what makes the suite feel finished. Resist the unified-manager-popup idea - it is more architecture than five single-purpose extensions warrant.
